title: González Garza to "John McCarty" (Adolfo González), El Paso, 29 March 1911 (CEHM-Carso CMXV.15.1432.1-4): read with the archive's "Clave G.A." card, validated on period decipherments

documents.shelfmark: CEHM-Carso, Fondo CMXV (Archivo Federico González Garza), CMXV.15.1432.1-4
documents.route: Federico González Garza (El Paso, Texas) -> "John McCarty" = Adolfo González (San Antonio, Texas)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the sheet; not in the typed list of period decipherments CMXV.18.1795.1; the CEHM record says "en clave".

transcription.source: Brice Dudout, from the CEHM viewer image (study copy, not redistributed)
transcription.notes: Typed sender's copy on a Texas Telegraph Company form; six coded words, the rest clear Spanish.

system.summary: Digraphic table of 2 rows x 15 columns (the "Clave G.A." card): a plain letter is one of five row letters (WZCTG or MVPKI) followed by its column letter (BLRAFQENHDXYOSJ).

prior_solution.where: The key card "Clave G.A. (una de las usadas en San Antonio)", CMXV.16.1557.1 scans 12-13, in the same fonds; no decipherment of this telegram on the sheet or in CMXV.18.1795.1.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout directed the work and decided what to publish; Claude (Opus) transcribed the card and the telegrams from the CEHM viewer images, ran the preregistered measure and wrote the reading.

solution.what: Telegram and key card transcribed from the CEHM viewer images; hashed before any key was tried.

The "Clave G.A." card (CMXV.16.1557.1 scans 12-13) selected among the fonds' cards on the first half of the coded letters; it decodes all six coded words (Galeana, Dr, Ag, Guerrero, Chih, Encinillas), two pairs faulty in transmission.
First held-out measure on two telegrams: 30 letters, car 0.833 vs best control 0.667: too short, not validated.

Preregistered measure run once: the card as is against the period decipherments of eight sibling telegrams, cipher transcribed blind; agreement 0.866 on 769 cipher letters vs at most 0.257 for 400 controls (VALIDATION.md).
Reading checked as Spanish sentences: 19 of 20 words read as sense; Ag not identified.

validation.notes: Six coded words are too few for the letter-model test. The key is the archive's card, validated separately against period decipherments of eight sibling telegrams (A = 0.866 on 769 cipher letters, controls at most 0.257; VALIDATION.md).

outcome.method_basis: The key is the archive's own card, applied unchanged; its fit to this traffic was tested against the period decipherments of sibling telegrams, not recovered from the ciphertext.

credits.note: transcription of CMXV.15.1432.1-4 and of the Clave G.A. card, reading, and validation of the card on eight sibling telegrams

gaps.detail: the letters are certain; the recipients' papers and Narváez 2011 and 2019 were not searched

gaps.item: whether the telegram is in print
gaps.detail: the books are not available to the project

gaps.item: a second reader's check of the transcriptions and of the card against the CEHM images
gaps.detail: the images may not be redistributed

outcome.notes: Read with the archive's Clave G.A. card; card validated on period decipherments of siblings. Earlier readings in the fonds with other cards: hernandez1911 (Echols), mexico1911 (Prabal Gupta).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Counted from reading.md: 19 of 20 words read as sense (16 sure, 3 with one faulty pair or an abbreviation resolved); Ag read as letters, not identified.

texts.label: Telegram of 29 March 1911 to John McCarty (CEHM-Carso CMXV.15.1432.1-4)
texts.summary: González Garza at El Paso to Adolfo González at San Antonio: on the 13th Dr (probably Madero) and Ag separated at Galeana, one towards Guerrero, the other towards Chihuahua, camping on the 23rd at Encinillas.

reading_review.note: Read as Spanish sentences: the six decoded words fill the gaps of the clear text (place names on the Galeana-Chihuahua road, Dr, Ag) and make coherent clauses; two faulty pairs corrected by the sense.
